Jazzfest Berlin 2026: Line-up Preview

By [Jazzfest Berlin](/festivals/jazzfest-berlin)

4/8/2026

Image

![](/sites/default/files/styles/image_square_large_contain/public/2026-08/Screenshot%202026-08-04%20alle%2016.48.45.png?itok=HoGF1cHo)

The 63rd edition of [Jazzfest Berlin](https://news.berlinerfestspiele.de/crm/service/t/BFS/3uFdTG/0/en/1S9/TVFS1x1DfD?preview=true) runs from 29 October to 1 November 2026 at the Haus der Berliner Festspiele and in its neighbouring venues A-Trane, Quasimodo and the Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church. The concert programme features 24 acts, including four world premieres, two European premieres and five German premieres. In total, over 130 artists from more than 25 countries, including international voices from the Berlin scene, are coming together to celebrate the global jazz community.  
  
The focus on community is also reflected in the cross-generational programme. The award-winning short film [*DREAM BABY DREAM*](https://news.berlinerfestspiele.de/crm/service/t/BFS/3uFdTG/0/en/1Sa/26SaODAeSR?preview=true) – shot as part of last year’s [Jazzfest Community Week](https://news.berlinerfestspiele.de/crm/service/t/BFS/3uFdTG/0/en/1Sb/OXR3xFfOTF?preview=true) with 60 children, teenagers and adults – premiered in Washington D.C. in late April and is screening at numerous music and film festivals both in Germany and abroad as well as at the opening of Jazzfest Berlin 2026 at the Haus der Berliner Festspiele.   
  
Once again, the line-up welcomes audiences to make new discoveries and features outstanding representatives from a variety of scenes, spanning a highly diverse cultural and musical landscape. At the same time, it celebrates two pioneering voices – Anthony Braxton and Alexander von Schlippenbach – who have shaped the global scene for decades including a regular presence at Jazzfest Berlin.  
  
And so 50 years after his [Jazzfest Berlin debut](https://news.berlinerfestspiele.de/crm/service/t/BFS/3uFdTG/0/en/1Sc/hi3hVRiWZX?preview=true) and seven years after his impressive [*Sonic Genome*](https://news.berlinerfestspiele.de/crm/service/t/BFS/3uFdTG/0/en/1Sd/ASOxJORii1?preview=true) at Gropius Bau, Braxton is back at the festival: in addition to the opening concert at the Haus der Berliner Festspiele with the Anthony Braxton Septet – formed especially for this occasion – he will also be leading a workshop over the course of several days for students at the Jazz Institut Berlin (JIB). Under the guidance of this style-defining composer and multi-instrumentalist, the students will come together to form the Creative Music Orchestra, and their concert in the Georg-Neumann-Saal at the JIB will be a highlight of this year’s Jazzfest Community Week.   
  
Alexander von Schlippenbach, who founded the groundbreaking [Globe Unity Orchestra](https://news.berlinerfestspiele.de/crm/service/t/BFS/3uFdTG/0/en/1Se/LSLfSPh19x?preview=true) in 1966 following a commission to compose for what was then called Berliner Jazztage, will bring the festival to a splendid close on Sunday at the Haus der Berliner Festspiele with an anniversary concert 60 years later – in the old formation, but with a new line-up of musicians including George Lewis, Aki Takase and Evan Parker.

**With**  
[Alexander Hawkins Willow Music](https://news.berlinerfestspiele.de/crm/service/t/BFS/3uFdTG/0/en/1QE/mRaJDJ3Z1S?preview=true) (European premiere)  
[Amir ElSaffar New Quartet](https://news.berlinerfestspiele.de/crm/service/t/BFS/3uFdTG/0/en/1QF/S99mSeFJFh?preview=true)  
[Anthony Braxton Septet](https://news.berlinerfestspiele.de/crm/service/t/BFS/3uFdTG/0/en/1QG/mRaJDJ3Z1S?preview=true) (World premiere)  
[Camila Nebbia Large Ensemble](https://news.berlinerfestspiele.de/crm/service/t/BFS/3uFdTG/0/en/1QH/S99mSeFJFh?preview=true): *the darkness, overwhelming and imposing, compelled me to light my own fires* (World premiere)  
[Ches Smith: *Clone Row*](https://news.berlinerfestspiele.de/crm/service/t/BFS/3uFdTG/0/en/1QI/eT2RRTDRDD?preview=true)

## World-class jazz since 1964

For jazz lovers, there's no better place to be in late autumn than Berlin, where one of Europe's most prestigious jazz festivals has been celebrating the genre in all its forms since 1964. Jazzfest Berlin offers a diverse array of performances, from classic jazz to experimental sounds. Over four days, the festival lights up venues across the city, bringing together top-tier international musicians, rising stars and a global audience of passionate jazz enthusiasts.

![JFB2025, Haus der Berliner Festspiele, Atmo](/system/files/styles/visitberlin_gallery_item_visitberlin_mobile_1x/private/datahub/images/genid-29fd6653e78d4000a34e3a26b7fe9a4e15667625-b7.jpg.jpg?itok=2GljKx6J "JFB2025, Haus der Berliner Festspiele, Atmo") 

JFB2025, Haus der Berliner Festspiele, Atmo

DREAM BABY DREAM

  

**From 29 October to 1 November, Jazzfest Berlin will showcase over 135 international musicians from more than 25 countries at Haus der Berliner Festspiele, A-Trane, Quasimodo and Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church.**

Under the artistic direction of **Nadin Deventer**, the 2026 edition of the festival will spotlight **24 acts – featuring four world premieres, two European premieres and five German premieres**, including works by Anthony Braxton, Alexander von Schlippenbach and the Globe Unity Orchestra, Camila Nebbia, Christian Lillinger and Wendy Eisenberg. The Jazzfest Community Week already begins on 26 October with workshops and neighbourhood concerts at the Jazz Institute Berlin and various venues in Berlin-Moabit.

  

**[Programme 2026](https://www.berlinerfestspiele.de/en/jazzfest-berlin/programm/2026)**

  

## Jazzfest Berlin at a glance

Originally known as the **Berliner Jazztage**, the Jazzfest Berlin was conceived as part of the Berliner Festwochen music festival. Due to its immense popularity, it soon became a standalone event and eventually **one of Europe's most prestigious jazz festivals**.

  

Held at venues such as the **Haus der Berliner Festspiele**, the iconic **Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church** and intimate jazz clubs like A-Trane and **Quasimodo**, Jazzfest Berlin offers visitors an **eclectic mix of musical experiences**. The festival spans traditional jazz, experimental performances and interdisciplinary collaborations, appealing to a wide range of tastes.

  

## Jazzfest Berlin highlights

* **Stellar lineup**: The festival attracts legendary jazz icons and rising stars alike. In previous years, greats like Miles Davis, Herbie Hancock and Ella Fitzgerald have graced the stage.

  

* **Diverse venues**: From the grand Haus der Berliner Festspiele to the intimate jazz clubs around the city, the variety of performance spaces adds a unique flavour to each event.

  

* **Experimental jazz**: Expect collaborations that mix jazz with electronic music, improvisation and other art forms.

  

* **Jazzfest Research Lab**: This innovative initiative brings together musicians, scholars and students to explore the history and evolution of jazz. This critical discourse includes workshops and presentations.

  

* **Concerts at Kaiser-Wilhelm-Gedächtniskirche**: Some of the most magical performances take place in this historic church, combining breathtaking acoustics and stunning architecture.

## Discover Jazzfest Berlin

Jazzfest Berlin is a **cultural institution** deeply rooted in Berlin's history. When it launched in 1964, it was meant to introduce the city to the transformative power of jazz, an art form associated with **innovation and freedom.**

# Jazzfest Berlin

[![Key Visual Jazzfest Berlin 2026](https://www.berlinerfestspiele.de/magnoliaPublic/dam/jcr:54357b4e-051f-4649-bc88-437b16ce98a2/jfb26_key_visual_2.300c9f6fc1ad5e7689f8edeb89ea07d7.svg)

## Concerts, Community & Outreach, Workshops, Films, Jam Sessions, Discourse](/en/jazzfest-berlin/programm/2026/kalender)

## Jazzfest Berlin 2026

DREAM BABY DREAM

![Word mark Jazzfest Berlin on a green background and below the sentence “Dream Baby Dream”](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.berlinerfestspiele.de%2FmagnoliaPublic%2F.imaging%2Ffocalpoint%2F16to9%2F1350%2Fdam%2Fjcr%3A9b35b75c-d30d-441c-8e09-01d00c1f06f8%2Fjfb26_trailer_thumbnail.webp&w=1440&q=75)

To this day, Berlin remains a refuge, a place of longing and a blank canvas for people from all over the world. This is especially true of the city’s international art and music scene, with its atmosphere of openness, diversity and constant renewal. This urban pluralism is eloquently expressed by the intergenerational short film *DREAM BABY DREAM*, created in collaboration with 60 Berliners as part of Jazzfest Berlin 2025 and providing its theme for 2026. This award-winning collective film project opens the 63rd festival edition at Haus der Berliner Festspiele and explores questions of belonging, utopia, dreams and trauma through music, movement and poetry.

Jazzfest Berlin has always seen itself as a place where tradition meets the future and local perspectives meet global experiences, hosting encounters between different communities, working methods and forms of expression. This year, Camila Nebbia, Mariá Portugal and ganavya – Berlin-based artists originally from Argentina, Brazil and the United States – embody this dialogue, moving effortlessly between continents, artistic scenes and musical languages. Christian Lillinger’s internationally cast world premiere *Open Form For Society II* presents a radically condensed form of chamber music, with five musicians exploring the bandleader’s intricate compositions on keyboard instruments. BONECRUSHER, an extraordinary orchestra led by Matthias Muche, brings together an impressive ensemble of 12 trombones at the Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church.

For six decades now, Anthony Braxton has explored liminal spaces, expanded aesthetic boundaries and invented new musical systems: “My music is like my life: It’s in between these areas.” Fifty years after his first appearance at the Berliner Jazztage and seven years after his remarkable *Sonic Genome* performance at Gropius Bau, the pioneering multi-instrumentalist, composer and educator returns to the Jazzfest Berlin with a septet created especially for this occasion: “What we call jazz is a sonic continuum. It’s not just about celebration of the past; it’s about the hope of the future.”

Over four days, the 2026 edition of the festival will bring together 24 acts featuring more than 135 musicians from over 25 countries, including four world premieres, two European premieres and five German premieres. Among the guests are some of the most influential voices in the international creative music scene, including the CHICAGO UNDERGROUND Duo, the Tomeka Reid Quartet, the ensemble Twin Talk, Clone Row led by the versatile drummer Ches Smith, the all-star trio Graewe/Drake/Jones and the visionary saxophonist Immanuel Wilkins’s acclaimed quartet, all from the United States. The human voice also plays a central role in this year’s programme. Artists such as Karoline Wallace, Alejandra Charry, Wendy Eisenberg and Amir ElSaffar move between song, improvisation and transcultural sonic research. Jazzfest Berlin welcomes two outstanding artists from the United Kingdom, Alexander Hawkins and Laura Jurd, as well as key figures of the Scandinavian scene, including Elin Forkelid and the ensemble (Exit) Knarr led by bassist Ingebrigt Håker Flaten. From Japan, Otomo Yoshihide joins the festival with his quintet, while Iranian clarinettist Shabnam Parvaresh presents her Sheen Trio at Jazzfest Berlin for the first time.

Creating spaces for encounters, experimentation and the inclusive, sometimes rebellious spirit of jazz, passing this on to future generations and engaging new audiences are at the heart of this year’s Jazzfest Community Week. As part of a multi-day workshop, 25 students from the Jazz Institute Berlin will immerse themselves in Braxton’s musical universe and join him to develop the JIB Creative Music Orchestra.
